subject: Clarify: Hosted API data retention, purge schedule and deletion proof
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@helioshealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: questions on retention + evidence request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached is our standard security questionnaire — we highlighted the items we need clarification on regarding hosted API data handling. Short version: we need to know where tenant data lives, retention TTLs, backup retention, and how deletion requests are handled (including evidence).

Questions we flagged:
1) For tenant-scoped data (chat history, prompts, embeddings), what is the default retention and can it be scoped per-tenant?
2) Are backups/snapshots retained in a way that prevents immediate deletion? If so, what is the window before data is removed from backups?
3) Do you store full request payloads (raw tokens) in any persistent logs/audit trails?
4) If we request a targeted erasure for a user or object id, what is the end-to-end timeline (primary store + backups + caches)?

We need answers for our compliance review by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Security & Privacy Manager
Helios Health

Attachment: Helios_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@helioshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on retention + evidence request

Hi Elena — thanks for the questionnaire and for flagging the priority items. Below is a high-level summary so your compliance team has something to work off quickly; we can follow with a short technical attestation and an SLA language proposal. I am attaching our deletion process doc for reference.

Quick answers (summary):
1) Default tenant-scoped retention: 30 days for generated content and request payloads on the hosted API. Yes — retention can be configured per-tenant (enterprise plans) via retention policy settings; we also support region-level retention controls.
2) Backups/snapshots: incremental snapshots are retained by default for 30 days. Backups add an additional 7–30 day window depending on snapshot cadence; by default, data in backups is eligible for purge within 30 days. We can offer shorter backup retention for Enterprise customers.
3) Persistent logs/audit trails: we retain structured audit events (request metadata, timestamps, route) for 90 days; we do not persist full raw tokens in long-term logging by default. Full request payloads are stored in primary tenant storage for the retention window above and cleared on deletion requests.
4) Targeted erasure timeline: primary store — typically removed within 72 hours after the erasure request is processed; caches evicted within minutes to hours; backups — removed during snapshot purge cycle (generally within 30 days), with an expedited path available. We can provide deletion evidence (audit entries + purge job logs) after completion.

Next steps: I can schedule a 30-min call with our infra lead (Aditya Rao) and product security to provide the formal attestation and a suggested contractual clause for the retention SLA. Does Thursday 10am PT work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachment: redwood-data-deletion-process-v1.2.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@helioshealth.com>

Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@helioshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: questions on retention + evidence request

Marissa — thanks for the quick summary, that helps. A couple of follow-ups from privacy and engineering:

- When you say "we do not persist full raw tokens in long-term logging by default" can you confirm whether full request payloads (user prompt + system prompt) are ever included in any centralized error logs or sampling traces? If yes, what's the retention for those samples?
- For targeted erasure we need the ability to request deletion by a three-legged user identifier (we will provide object IDs) and receive a signed confirmation that includes timestamps and the storage locations cleared.
- Backup expunge: can you confirm whether backups are retained in the same region as primary data or whether cross-region replication could leave copies in other jurisdictions? This impacts our data residency controls.

If you can capture these in the attestation and provide a sample signed proof, that'll be ideal.

—Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Aditya / Neha — looping you both in to confirm the technical timelines and the attestation language for Helios Health. Elena's team needs explicit confirmation on:
1) whether sampled traces ever contain full request payloads and their retention window;
2) confirmation of cross-region replication behavior for backups and whether we can lock backups to a single region for this customer;
3) an expedited deletion path and what evidence/artifact we can return (signed log of purge jobs, dataset ids, timestamps).

Aditya — can you provide the concrete timeline we can commit to (primary store, caches, backups) and the mechanistic description we can put in a signed attestation? Neha — can you confirm what we can offer contractually (expedited backup purge SLA, attestation delivery cadence) for enterprise customers?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@helioshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 16:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API: questions on retention + evidence request

Hi all — below are the technical answers we can include in the formal attestation. I tried to be specific so Helios has a clear operational picture. Happy to join a call for clarifications.

1) Centralized logs and sampled traces:
- Error traces / sampling: we do sample request payloads in a limited fashion for post-mortem/debugging. Sampling is opt-in at the tenant level and defaults to OFF for new tenants.
- If enabled, sampled traces that include payloads are retained for a maximum of 14 days and are stored in an access-controlled diagnostics index (not in long-lived audit tables). We can disable sampling for Helios entirely or set a custom retention window.

2) Primary storage and caches:
- Primary tenant store: request payloads and generated outputs are persisted to the tenant's primary storage cluster per the tenant retention policy (default 30 days). On erasure request we mark objects soft-deleted immediately and enqueue them for purge; primary-store purge jobs run continuously and complete within 72 hours in >95% of cases.
- KV caches / in-memory caches: ephemeral and evicted within seconds to minutes once an object is deleted or TTL expires.

3) Backups and snapshots:
- Snapshot model: we take incremental snapshots (regionally scoped) with a 24h cadence. Snapshots are retained for a default of 30 days. Snapshots are stored in the same region as the primary tenant by default; cross-region replication is only enabled when customers opt into geo-redundancy. For Helios, we can lock snapshot storage to a single region to satisfy residency constraints.
- Expedited backup purge: we have an expedited workflow that flags relevant snapshots for higher-priority purge. Standard removal from backup rotation is bounded by the snapshot retention window; with expedited processing and a premium support ticket we can reduce backup removal to within 7 days.

4) Evidence & attestation:
- Deletion evidence: we can provide a signed artifact containing: identifiers of purged objects, timestamps (soft-delete processed, primary purge completed, backup purge initiated), and purge-job log ids. The artifact is cryptographically signed by our infra service account and stored in a customer-only S3 location (or delivered via secure Drive link).
- Formal attestation: we can produce a one-off attestation doc signed by Product Security that captures the tenant's retention settings, snapshot policy, and guaranteed timelines under the selected SLA.

Contractual options (Neha): for Enterprise customers we can:
- Commit to 30-day backup retention by default, with an option to contract a 7-day backup purge SLA with an associated fee/commit.
- Guarantee deletion evidence delivery within 7 business days after purge completion as part of the attestation pack.

I'll draft the attestation language and the technical appendix this week. Marissa — if Helios needs the attestation in DocuSign form, we can produce that version as well.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
